protocol.note_mapping: on=round(48000*(offset+scale*source_start)); gate=round(48000*scale*source_gate); off=on+gate. This separate gate rounding exactly preserves the established baseline; it can differ by one sample from rounding mapped source end.
protocol.program_mapping: All100 inferred program changes use round(48000*(offset+scale*timeline.midi_start_seconds)). The old timeline audio_start_seconds is not reused for corrected maps. Bar-based program inference remains an assumption, not measured MIDI command time.
protocol.event_order: Sort by frame, then patch, old off, new on; preserve source-file order within each category. Patch changes preserve existing held/release voices.
protocol.score_windows: Exactly the100 prior v4 absolute recording-time windows, unchanged for every map/model. No moved or reselected windows.

protocol.metric: Unchanged frozen stereo_metrics.py: one stereo-pair RMS normalization;64 bands80-14000Hz;STFT512/2048/8192. No local or per-model timing, phase, pitch, frequency or gain optimization beyond established pair RMS normalization.
protocol.analysis: All12 outcomes; every100-row metric; model contrasts within each map; difference-in-differences vs old mapping; per-patch ranking reversals and all100/target ranking stability. No adoption threshold or score-based winner selection.
limitations: Reused recording/windows and prior calibrated DSP candidates, not a fresh holdout.
Changing maps jointly moves notes, gates and inferred program commands; it does not isolate physical MIDI latency from program inference or allocation history.
Recorded chorus remains an audio-time capture model; internal global LFO starts at time0. Event shifts therefore also change their phase at note arrival without any phase fitting.
The research Reverb candidate retains96dB retirement,12voice oldest replacement and48tick stolen fade; hardware allocator remains unverified.
